title: Georg Adam Starhemberg (Paris) to the Austrian envoy at Madrid, 23 May 1758 (Pillon collection; Cryptiana)

documents.shelfmark: Alexandre Pillon collection (no archive shelfmark known); transcribed on Cryptiana variable2.htm
documents.route: Georg Adam Starhemberg (Paris) -> Austrian envoy at Madrid [Rosenberg?]

plaintext.source: No clear copy or decipherment known; the clear opening and closing frame the cipher.

transcription.source: Tomokiyo's Cryptiana transcription from Pillon's image (1,721 digits) plus five digits read by the contributor of issue #555 from manuscript photographs
transcription.notes: No image in the project's hands; the photographs are Pillon's and not shareable. Tomokiyo's digits re-fetched 14 Nov 2026 agree with the contributor's apart from the five insertions. Length: 1,726 digits (symbols); 413 units in the contributor's parse (units.txt, measured: 413 tokens, 223 distinct).

system.summary: Austrian two-table numeric code of 1752 (Clavis Prima and Secunda), figures written without break: 2-digit and 5-digit (31xxx) units, with switch, control and null units.
system.notes: Key per the contributor: DECODE R1695 and R1698 (1752 tables), R1696/R1697 instructions and worked examples; not checked here.

prior_solution.where: Tomokiyo, Cryptiana variable2.htm, lists it as non-decrypted; one web search 14 Nov 2026 found nothing

conditions.human_role: Contributed result (GitHub issue #555, aaymeloglu): the contributor matched the 1752 tables to the digit stream and checked the photographs; the project only checked and filed it. The contributor names OpenAI Codex as the tool used.
tools: two-table parse and alignment (contributor's run_checks.py, not run here)

solution.what: By the contributor (issue #555, by the contributor's record): the 1752 Austrian Prima/Secunda tables (DECODE R1695/R1698) applied to Tomokiyo's digits; two-table parse matched to the stream; five digits added from the photographs.

Integration check: Tomokiyo's 1,721 digits re-fetched; difflib shows exactly three line-end insertions (1+2+2) in the contributor's 1,726; own_check.py: the 413 units cover the stream exactly, 389 agree with the contributor's tables, 14 are documented alternatives or values missing from their tsv excerpt; key tables and photographs not checked.
Strict count of the German reading of the cipher passage (aaymeloglu/edition.md): 170 of 188 words = 90.4% (restored letters, [?] words and the defective 119 as holes).
Cryptiana (non-decrypted), catalogue.json and leads.json (not listed), one web search (Starhemberg 1758 Farinelli Minorca cipher): no prior decipherment found.

texts.summary: Starhemberg hopes the memorandum given to Wall will bring Spain into the war or towards an honourable peace, reads the matching statements of Farinelli and Wall as a sign that the cession of Minorca would bring Spain in against England and Prussia, and tells the envoy to keep working on Wall until the courier Zinner arrives.
